entries.name: d3-delaunay
entries.purpose: Delaunay triangulation and Voronoi diagrams of 2D points.

entries.name: earcut
entries.purpose: Fast triangulation of 2D polygons with holes (for filling shapes).

entries.name: simplex-noise
entries.purpose: 2D/3D/4D simplex noise on the CPU (shaders can use ctx.utils.glsl instead).

entries.name: Matter.js
entries.purpose: 2D rigid-body physics: bodies, constraints, collisions.

entries.name: opentype.js
entries.purpose: Read fonts and turn text into vector paths (outlines, points along glyphs).

entries.name: MediaPipe Tasks Vision
entries.purpose: Hand, face and pose landmarks, segmentation and object detection in the browser (WASM + GPU).
entries.notes: Models download from storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-models; see the hand-tracking example.

entries.name: ONNX Runtime Web
entries.purpose: Run ONNX models in the browser on WebGPU or WASM.
entries.notes: Weights come with each model and have their own licenses.

entries.name: glTF Transform
entries.purpose: Read and edit glTF/GLB files (meshes, materials) in the scene.

entries.name: culori
entries.purpose: Color spaces and interpolation (OKLCH, Lab, palettes, gradients).

entries.name: Tone.js
entries.purpose: Synthesize and sequence sound in the browser (synths, effects, transport).

entries.name: Meyda
entries.purpose: Audio features (MFCC, chroma, spectral centroid…) beyond ctx.audio's bands.

entries.name: trimesh
entries.purpose: Load, build, repair and export triangle meshes (OBJ, GLB, STL); booleans and sampling.

entries.name: Shapely
entries.purpose: 2D geometry operations: buffers, unions, intersections, simplification.

entries.name: vpype
entries.purpose: Prepare SVGs for pen plotters: merge and sort lines, page layout, multiple layers.

entries.name: OpenCV (opencv-python-headless)
entries.purpose: Image and video processing: filters, edges, contours, optical flow, feature detection.

entries.name: scikit-image
entries.purpose: Image analysis: segmentation, morphology, contour finding, transforms.

entries.name: Pillow
entries.purpose: Read, write and edit images (resize, crop, draw, formats).

entries.name: librosa
entries.purpose: Music analysis: beats, tempo, onsets, pitch, spectrograms.

entries.name: Open3D
entries.purpose: Point clouds and meshes: reconstruction, registration, normals.

entries.name: NetworkX
entries.purpose: Graphs and networks: layouts, shortest paths, generators.

entries.name: svgpathtools
entries.purpose: Read SVG paths and sample, measure or transform them.

entries.name: PyMeshLab
entries.purpose: MeshLab filters from Python: remeshing, decimation, smoothing.
entries.notes: GPL: fine to run; distributing code built on it carries GPL terms.

entries.name: FFmpeg
entries.purpose: Convert, cut and combine video and audio; extract frames; encode.
entries.notes: Builds with GPL parts are GPL.

entries.name: Blender
entries.purpose: Render or process 3D scenes headless (blender -b -P script.py).

entries.name: OpenSCAD
entries.purpose: Script solid 3D models (CSG) and export STL.

entries.name: ImageMagick
entries.purpose: Convert and batch-edit images from the command line.

entries.name: Inkscape
entries.purpose: Convert and export SVG (PDF, PNG), text to paths, from the command line.

entries.name: Potrace
entries.purpose: Trace bitmaps into smooth vector outlines (SVG).

entries.name: Depth Anything V2
entries.purpose: Depth maps from a single image.
entries.gpu: optional (CUDA or MPS; slow on CPU)

entries.name: rembg
entries.purpose: Remove image backgrounds (cut-out with alpha).

entries.name: Segment Anything (SAM)
entries.purpose: Masks for any object from points or boxes.

entries.name: Whisper
entries.purpose: Speech to text with timestamps (subtitles, lyrics timing).

entries.name: Demucs
entries.purpose: Split music into stems: drums, bass, vocals, other.

entries.name: Real-ESRGAN
entries.purpose: Upscale images and video frames 2–4x.

entries.name: Diffusers (Stable Diffusion and others)
entries.purpose: Generate or edit images with diffusion models.
entries.weights_license: depends on the model (e.g. CreativeML OpenRAIL-M, which restricts some uses)

entries.name: poisson-disk-sampling
entries.purpose: Poisson disk sampling in any dimension, with a distance function for variable density and point-by-point generation.

entries.name: d3-contour
entries.purpose: Isolines and filled contour polygons from a grid of values (marching squares), plus density contours of points.

entries.name: Perfect Freehand
entries.purpose: Turns pointer or pen samples into the outline polygon of a pressure-sensitive, tapered freehand stroke.

entries.name: Bezier.js
entries.purpose: Quadratic and cubic Bezier curve math: points, normals, offsets, outlines, intersections, projection and bounding boxes.

entries.name: Rough.js
entries.purpose: Draws lines, shapes and paths in a sketchy hand-drawn style with hachure, cross-hatch and other fills on a 2D canvas or SVG.

entries.name: Paper.js
entries.purpose: Vector graphics scripting with a scene graph of paths, including boolean operations (unite, intersect, subtract, exclude), smoothing and flattening.

entries.name: TactileJS
entries.purpose: Describes and places the 81 isohedral tiling types, so custom tile shapes with matching edges cover the plane, with a colouring for each copy.

entries.name: Flubber
entries.purpose: Smooth interpolation between 2D shapes with different point counts, plus splitting one shape into many and combining many into one.

entries.name: Trianglify
entries.purpose: Generates low-poly triangle patterns from jittered points with ColorBrewer gradients, as geometry, SVG or canvas.

entries.name: Clipper2 (clipper2-ts)
entries.purpose: Polygon boolean operations (union, intersection, difference, xor) and offsetting with round, miter, square or bevel joins, ported from Angus Johnson's Clipper2.

entries.name: Three.js
entries.purpose: Full 3D engine (scene graph, PBR materials, lights, shadows) that can render into the scene's own WebGL2 context.

entries.name: regl
entries.purpose: Functional, declarative wrapper around WebGL draw calls that runs on an existing GL context.

entries.name: OGL
entries.purpose: Minimal WebGL framework with a scene graph, primitives and programs, close to raw GL.

entries.name: glMatrix
entries.purpose: Fast vector, matrix and quaternion math for WebGL transforms and cameras.

entries.name: JSCAD modeling
entries.purpose: Parametric CAD in JavaScript: primitives, CSG booleans, extrusions and transforms producing polygon solids.

entries.name: Manifold
entries.purpose: Fast, robust WebAssembly mesh booleans (CSG) that always return watertight manifold meshes.

entries.name: isosurface
entries.purpose: Extracts triangle meshes from scalar fields with marching cubes, marching tetrahedra or surface nets.

entries.name: cannon-es
entries.purpose: Lightweight 3D rigid-body physics engine in plain JavaScript.

entries.name: Rapier
entries.purpose: Fast deterministic 3D physics engine written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly.

entries.name: three-mesh-bvh
entries.purpose: Bounding volume hierarchy for Three.js meshes, for fast raycasting and spatial queries against dense geometry.

entries.name: chroma.js
entries.purpose: Color conversions and color scales (Lab/LCh/OKLCH interpolation, Bézier scales, lightness correction, ColorBrewer palettes).

entries.name: d3-scale-chromatic
entries.purpose: Scientific and ColorBrewer color maps (Viridis, Magma, Turbo, RdBu, ...) as interpolators and schemes.

entries.name: HSLuv
entries.purpose: Perceptually uniform HSL (HSLuv and pastel HPLuv) to and from sRGB, for palettes with even lightness.

entries.name: image-q
entries.purpose: Reduce an image to a small palette (Wu, NeuQuant, RgbQuant) and remap it with dithering (Floyd-Steinberg, Atkinson, ...).

entries.name: imagetracerjs
entries.purpose: Trace raster images into vector paths (lines and quadratic curves per color layer) or SVG.

entries.name: TinySDF
entries.purpose: Render font glyphs to signed distance fields in the browser for crisp, scalable text with outlines and glow in shaders.

entries.name: Hydra
entries.purpose: Live-coding video synth: chain oscillators, noise, feedback and canvas/video sources into WebGL visuals on its own canvas.
entries.notes: AGPL-3.0: fetched at runtime from the CDN, not bundled; distributing code built on it carries AGPL terms.

entries.name: p5.js
entries.purpose: Processing-style creative coding (shapes, noise, color, typography) in instance mode, drawn into an offscreen p5.Graphics.

entries.name: Pts
entries.purpose: Creative-coding geometry (points, lines, polygons, convex hulls, intersections, grids) with a CanvasForm that draws on any 2D context.

entries.name: glur
entries.purpose: Fast Gaussian blur of RGBA or 16-bit grey pixel arrays on the CPU (IIR, cost independent of radius).

entries.name: d3-force
entries.purpose: Force-directed simulation of particles and graphs: collision, links, centering, radial and positional forces.

entries.name: ngraph.forcelayout
entries.purpose: Fast 2D/3D force-directed layout for large graphs (Barnes–Hut), used with ngraph.graph.

entries.name: lindenmayer
entries.purpose: L-systems: rewrites strings with deterministic, stochastic, context-sensitive or parametric productions for procedural plants and fractals.

entries.name: PathFinding.js
entries.purpose: Grid pathfinding: A*, Dijkstra, best-first, breadth-first, jump point and bidirectional finders.

entries.name: planck.js
entries.purpose: 2D rigid-body physics (a JavaScript port of Box2D) with joints, chains, motors and continuous collision.

entries.name: spectral.js
entries.purpose: Pigment-like color mixing with Kubelka–Munk theory, so blue and yellow make green.

entries.name: d3-hexbin
entries.purpose: Bins 2D points into a hexagonal grid and returns each bin's center and members.

entries.name: Flatbush
entries.purpose: Fast static spatial index (packed Hilbert R-tree) for box and nearest-neighbor queries over many points or rectangles.

entries.name: tween.js
entries.purpose: Tweens object properties over time with easing functions, delays, chaining and repeats.

entries.name: SunCalc
entries.purpose: Sun and moon position (altitude, azimuth), sunrise/sunset/twilight times and moon phase for any place and time.

entries.name: PyMCubes
entries.purpose: Marching cubes: turn an implicit field or voxel volume into a triangle mesh.

entries.name: circlify
entries.purpose: Circle packing of flat or nested data into a circle, for bubble charts and hierarchy maps.

entries.name: UMAP
entries.purpose: Dimensionality reduction that lays out high-dimensional data as 2D or 3D points that keep neighborhoods together.

entries.name: REBOUND
entries.purpose: N-body gravity integrator for orbits, planetary systems, flybys and disks.

entries.name: python-sgp4
entries.purpose: Satellite positions from TLE orbital elements with the standard SGP4 propagator, for orbits and ground tracks.

entries.name: hilbertcurve
entries.purpose: Hilbert space-filling curves in any dimension: point order, index ↔ coordinates.

entries.name: meanderpy
entries.purpose: Simulates meandering rivers migrating over time, with cutoffs that leave oxbow lakes.

entries.name: WebGL Fluid Simulation
entries.purpose: GPU stable-fluids shaders (advection, pressure, vorticity, splats, bloom) for interactive ink-in-water simulations; adapted into the scene rather than imported.
entries.notes: The shaders are ported into the scene (see the example); the CDN link is the source they come from.

entries.name: Anime.js
entries.purpose: Animates values of any JS object with timelines, staggered delays (grids, origins) and a large set of easings.

entries.name: PixiJS
entries.purpose: Fast GPU 2D renderer (batched sprites and particles, blend modes, blur/displacement filters, render textures) that can render into the scene's own WebGL2 context.
entries.notes: Import the jsDelivr build: esm.sh's build drops PixiJS's side-effect modules, so particles and filters never register.

entries.name: Babylon.js
entries.purpose: Full 3D engine (PBR materials, image-based lighting, shadows, GPU particles, post-processing pipeline) that can render into the scene's own WebGL2 context.

entries.name: WaveFunctionCollapse
entries.purpose: Fills a grid with tiles or pixels that follow local adjacency rules, collapsing the lowest-entropy cell and propagating constraints (JS port of mxgmn's algorithm).

entries.name: Lottie Web
entries.purpose: Plays Lottie (After Effects/Bodymovin JSON) vector animations, rendering to SVG or canvas frame by frame.

entries.name: Shan Shui Infinite
entries.purpose: Procedural, infinitely scrolling Chinese landscape painting (mountains, trees, architecture, boats) generated as SVG polylines; its generator is fetched from a pinned commit and run in the scene.

entries.name: fishdraw
entries.purpose: Procedurally generated fish (body, scales, fins, eye and a made-up binomial name) as pen-plotter polylines; fetched from a pinned commit and run in the scene.

entries.name: MarkovJunior
entries.purpose: Probabilistic programming language of grid rewrite rules that grows mazes, rivers, dungeons and plants (core ported to JS in the scene).
entries.notes: The interpreter is ported into the example's scene; its models come from the repository's models/ folder.

entries.name: Lenia
entries.purpose: Continuous cellular automata with lifelike gliding creatures; rule and species catalog (run as GPU shaders in the scene).
entries.notes: The update rule runs as shaders in the example's scene; species (e.g. Orbium) come from animals.json.

entries.name: Growing Neural Cellular Automata
entries.purpose: Pretrained neural cellular automata that grow an emoji from one seed cell and regenerate after damage (run as GPU shaders in the scene).
entries.notes: The update rule (Sobel perception, 48→128→16 network, stochastic update, alive masking) runs as shaders in the example's scene; weights for 10 regenerating emoji models were extracted from models.zip into the example's nca-weights.bin.

entries.name: Primitive
entries.purpose: Reproduces an image with translucent geometric shapes found by random search and hill climbing (ported to JavaScript in the scene).
entries.notes: Go program; the example ports core.go, worker.go, optimize.go and the triangle/rectangle/ellipse shapes to JavaScript and runs the search within a time budget per frame.

entries.name: sandspiel
entries.purpose: Falling-sand game with many interacting elements (sand, water, fire, plants, lava, ice, gas…); rules ported to JavaScript in the scene.
entries.notes: Rust→WASM original; the example ports species.rs/lib.rs rules and the sand.glsl palette to JavaScript/GLSL, with a simplified CPU wind field in place of the GPU fluid.

entries.name: Slime-Simulation
entries.purpose: Physarum slime mould agent simulation: agents sense, follow and deposit trails that diffuse and decay into vein networks, with several competing species (Unity compute shaders ported to WebGL2 in the scene).
entries.notes: Unity/HLSL original; the example ports SlimeSim.compute's kernels to GLSL (agents in float textures, deposit as additive points) and uses the presets in Assets/Settings. GPL-3.0 (copyleft).

entries.name: Black Hole Shader
entries.purpose: Real-time Schwarzschild black hole: gravitational lensing of stars and an accretion disc with Doppler and beaming, via precomputed ray-deflection tables (ported to WebGL2 in the scene).
entries.notes: functions.glsl and model.glsl are ported into the example's shader; the C++ table precomputation (preprocess/functions.cc) is ported to JavaScript and runs at startup. The Gaia star maps are replaced by a procedural sky.

entries.name: animal-proc-anim
entries.purpose: Procedural animation of a fish, snake and lizard: distance-constrained joint chains with angle limits, FABRIK legs, smooth filled body outlines. A Processing (Java) sketch; port its few files to JS.
entries.notes: Processing source, not runnable in the browser: port Chain.pde/Util.pde (resolve, fabrikResolve, constrainAngle) and the creature classes; curveVertex is Catmull-Rom (bezier controls p1+(p2-p0)/6, p2-(p3-p1)/6). Resolves once per frame at 60 fps, so step it at a fixed 1/60 s.

entries.name: Nonflowers
entries.purpose: Procedurally generated paintings of nonexistent flowers in a Chinese painting style (woody or herbaceous plants, leaves, petals, paper texture) drawn with Canvas 2D; main.js is fetched from a pinned commit and run in a worker with the DOM stubbed.
entries.notes: Plain script that patches Array.prototype (.x/.y/.z/[-1]) and Math.random and uses document.createElement('canvas'); run it in a Web Worker via new Function with window/document/Math stubs and OffscreenCanvas. Its per-pixel Layer.filter/bound are slow (~1 s at 1200 px); skip transparent pixels. Seeds match the site's ?seed= when you paint the background paper first like its load().

entries.name: differential-line
entries.purpose: Differential growth of a closed line: vertices attract their neighbours, repel nearby vertices and split long edges, folding into brain-coral shapes; Python/Cython, ported to JS in the example's scene.
entries.notes: Cython original (needs compiling); the scene ports optimize_position/__reject, split_edge, spawn and the zonemap grid to JS.

entries.name: space-colonization
entries.purpose: Space colonization (Runions et al. 2007): bud tips grow toward scattered attractor points, splitting as they go, for trees, roots and leaf venation; returns the bud graph each iteration.
entries.notes: License is stated as MIT in the README and package.json (the repo has no LICENSE file). Its iterate() looks up parents with indexOf on every call (O(n^2)); keep bud counts in the low thousands or memoize indexOf during the call.

entries.name: dlaf
entries.purpose: Fast diffusion-limited aggregation in 2D or 3D: random walkers stick to a growing cluster (coral, frost, lightning forms), with spacing, attraction distance, stickiness and stubbornness parameters and hooks for starting positions and motion.
entries.notes: C++ (needs Boost for its R-tree); not runnable in the browser as is. The dlaf example ports dlaf.cpp's Model to JavaScript with a uniform grid in place of the R-tree; reuse that port for scenes.

entries.name: sand-spline
entries.purpose: Anders Hoff's sand-painted splines: control points random-walk with growing noise while faint grains are scattered along the interpolating spline; Python, ported to JS/GLSL in the example's scene.
entries.notes: Python (numpy/scipy) original; the scene reimplements SandSpline and the circle/circles/hlines layouts, replacing scipy's splprep/splev with a chord-length Catmull-Rom spline.

entries.name: concaveman
entries.purpose: Concaveman wraps an original point cloud in a concave hull. Concavity controls how closely its boundary follows the points.

entries.name: Simplify.js
entries.purpose: Simplify.js reduces a noisy polyline with Douglas–Peucker simplification. The original line remains visible for comparison.

entries.name: adaptive-bezier-curve
entries.purpose: adaptive-bezier-curve subdivides a cubic curve more finely near bends. Quality changes its adaptive sampling scale.

entries.name: Martinez polygon clipping
entries.purpose: Martinez computes boolean operations between a star and a movable disk, including holes in the resulting polygon.

entries.name: PolyBool
entries.purpose: PolyBool combines the regions of two polygons with union, intersection, difference and XOR.

entries.name: chaikin-smooth
entries.purpose: Chaikin smoothing repeatedly cuts corners from an open zigzag. Endpoints remain fixed while the path rounds out.

entries.name: cdt2d
entries.purpose: cdt2d creates a constrained Delaunay mesh around a courtyard. Boundary edges and the hole remain intact.

entries.name: pack-spheres
entries.purpose: pack-spheres grows circles while keeping them separate. A fixed random seed makes comparisons reproducible.

entries.name: d3-shape
entries.purpose: D3 Shape draws the same sample points with six curve interpolators, from straight segments to smooth natural splines.

entries.name: svg-mesh-3d
entries.purpose: svg-mesh-3d converts an original cubic SVG leaf into an indexed triangle mesh. Sampling quality changes the boundary detail.

entries.name: alpha-shape
entries.purpose: alpha-shape extracts the boundary of an alpha complex. Increasing Alpha rejects larger circumcircles and can split the boundary.

entries.name: polyline-normals
entries.purpose: polyline-normals computes vertex normals and miter lengths for a zigzag ribbon. Width moves its two sides along those normals.

entries.name: Delaunator
entries.purpose: Delaunator triangulates an original point cloud. Each triangle gets a color while the points remain visible on request.

entries.name: fit-curve
entries.purpose: fit-curve approximates a noisy sampled stroke with cubic Bézier segments. Error controls the fitting tolerance.

entries.name: monotone-convex-hull-2d
entries.purpose: monotone-convex-hull-2d finds the convex hull indices of a point cloud using a monotone chain.

entries.name: robust-point-in-polygon
entries.purpose: robust-point-in-polygon classifies a movable probe and a grid of points as inside, outside or on the polygon boundary.

entries.name: poly-decomp.js
entries.purpose: poly-decomp decomposes a concave star into convex polygons with quickDecomp. Explode separates the resulting pieces for inspection.

entries.name: rectangle-decomposition
entries.purpose: rectangle-decomposition partitions a rectilinear region into non-overlapping rectangles. A movable courtyard remains empty.

entries.name: extrude-polyline
entries.purpose: extrude-polyline builds a triangle mesh for a thick polyline with miter or bevel joins and butt or square caps.

entries.name: polygon-offset
entries.purpose: polygon-offset computes rounded parallel outlines of an original concave polygon. Distance changes the offset margin.

entries.name: b-spline
entries.purpose: b-spline evaluates a rational B-spline with de Boor’s algorithm. Degree changes continuity and Weight pulls the curve toward one control point.

entries.name: polylabel
entries.purpose: Polylabel searches for the point farthest from a polygon’s edges and hole. The circle shows its clearance from the boundary.

entries.name: potpack
entries.purpose: Potpack packs rectangles into a compact texture atlas. Colors track each rectangle and Fill reports occupied area.

entries.name: robust-predicates
entries.purpose: robust-predicates evaluates orient2d for points around a directed line. The moving probe displays the signed orientation result.

entries.name: box-intersect
entries.purpose: box-intersect reports overlapping pairs in a moving set of axis-aligned boxes. Matching pairs are connected at their centers.

entries.name: d3-polygon
entries.purpose: D3 Polygon measures area, perimeter and centroid of a changing polygon. The bright point marks its geometric centroid.

entries.name: barycentric
entries.purpose: barycentric computes coordinates relative to a triangle. The three weights become red, green and blue for the probe and the interior grid.

entries.name: streamlines
entries.purpose: Streamlines integrates an original vector field with RK4 while keeping paths apart. Four spacing settings are computed when the scene opens.

entries.name: d3-random
entries.purpose: D3 Random samples seeded distributions and bins them into a histogram. The sample count is preserved, including the two overflow bins.

entries.name: d3-color
entries.purpose: D3 Color converts CIELCH coordinates to display RGB. Gray crosses mark colors outside the sRGB gamut before display clipping.

entries.name: d3-interpolate
entries.purpose: D3 Interpolate blends the same colors in RGB, Lab, HCL and Cubehelix. The moving marker samples the same fraction in every color space.

entries.name: d3-ease
entries.purpose: D3 Ease remaps progress through linear, cubic, bounce, back and elastic curves. A manual progress control keeps overshoot and endpoint behavior easy to inspect.

entries.name: bezier-easing
entries.purpose: Bezier Easing solves a cubic timing curve from its two control points. Pink handles show the curve and the mint point shows the solved progress.

entries.name: d3-hierarchy
entries.purpose: D3 Hierarchy lays out the same weighted hierarchy as a treemap or packed circles. Synthetic groups and values are generated from a fixed seed.

entries.name: d3-sankey
entries.purpose: D3 Sankey computes node positions and flow widths for an original three-stage resource network. Changing the branch share preserves the total flow.

entries.name: d3-chord
entries.purpose: D3 Chord converts an original exchange matrix into arcs and ribbons. The highlight control dims unrelated exchanges.

entries.name: d3-quadtree
entries.purpose: D3 Quadtree partitions seeded points into cells and finds the point nearest a query within a radius. Empty searches are shown explicitly.

entries.name: RBush
entries.purpose: RBush indexes original rectangles in an R-tree and returns the ones intersecting the orange search window.

entries.name: KDBush
entries.purpose: KDBush indexes a fixed point set in a flat KD-tree. A radius query highlights every point inside the orange circle.

entries.name: flatqueue
entries.purpose: FlatQueue stores points with their distance as priority and pops the nearest points first. Numbered dots show the queue order.

entries.name: Supercluster
entries.purpose: Supercluster builds zoom-dependent clusters from 360 original geographic points. Bubble numbers show how many source points each cluster represents.

entries.name: fft.js
entries.purpose: FFT.js transforms a synthetic two-frequency signal into a spectrum. No microphone or audio playback is required.

entries.name: MarchingSquaresJS
entries.purpose: MarchingSquares.js extracts isolines from an original scalar field. Contour spacing and the height of the second peak reshape the terrain drawing.

entries.name: FloBezier
entries.purpose: FloBezier calculates curve length and inverts arc length to place evenly spaced samples. The gray dots use uniform parameter steps for comparison.

entries.name: Numeric.js · ODE
entries.purpose: Numeric.js integrates a damped oscillator with adaptive Dormand–Prince steps. The phase portrait shows position against velocity; the marker follows the computed solution.

entries.name: Color.js
entries.purpose: Color.js interpolates between two original colors in sRGB, OKLCH or Lab and converts the result to display sRGB. The lower row shows the chosen midpoint.

entries.name: d3-geo
entries.purpose: D3 Geo projects a spherical graticule and original evenly distributed markers. Rotation reveals how orthographic, stereographic and equirectangular projections differ.

entries.name: d3-geo-projection
entries.purpose: D3 Geo Projection draws the same spherical grid with four additional world projections. All markers are original synthetic coordinates.

entries.name: Graphology
entries.purpose: Graphology stores an original undirected network and queries neighbors and degrees. Choose a node to highlight exactly its immediate connections.

entries.name: ngraph.path
entries.purpose: ngraph.path finds the least-cost route across an original grid. The central road has a variable toll; a zero heuristic makes A* an exact weighted shortest-path search.

entries.name: Cytoscape.js
entries.purpose: Cytoscape computes a breadth-first layout and breadth-first traversal of an original directed network. Highlight depth reveals the discovered layers.

entries.name: MARTINI
entries.purpose: Martini creates an adaptive RTIN mesh from a 65 × 65 synthetic height grid. The refinement threshold controls triangle detail.

entries.name: delaunay-triangulate
entries.purpose: delaunay-triangulate computes a three-dimensional Delaunay tetrahedralization. Exploding the cells makes their four triangular faces visible.

entries.name: surface-nets
entries.purpose: Surface Nets extracts the level surface of a sampled sphere with a sinusoidal ripple. Resolution changes the sampling grid while Level changes the surface.

entries.name: mesh-laplacian
entries.purpose: mesh-laplacian computes cotangent weights for a triangle grid. Explicit diffusion steps spread a central heat pulse using that matrix.

entries.name: distance-transform
entries.purpose: Distance Transform computes the nearest seed distance using Euclidean, Manhattan or Chebyshev metrics. Bands make their different unit circles visible.

entries.name: ndarray-warp
entries.purpose: ndarray-warp inverse-maps a synthetic checkerboard through a swirl with linear interpolation. Zero twist reconstructs the source grid.

entries.name: Pixelmatch
entries.purpose: Pixelmatch compares two original RGBA drawings and highlights changed pixels. Threshold controls sensitivity to color differences as well as the shifted shape.

entries.name: d3-tricontour
entries.purpose: D3 Tricontour extracts filled contours from irregular points with scalar values. The points are generated locally and are not a regular raster grid.

entries.name: d3-geo-voronoi
entries.purpose: D3 Geo Voronoi partitions a sphere around synthetic sites. The orthographic view clips cells at the horizon while rotating the globe.

entries.name: TopoJSON Simplify
entries.purpose: TopoJSON Simplify reduces an original wavy border shared by two regions. The same topology arc is reused on both sides, preventing cracks.

entries.name: cannon.js
entries.purpose: Cannon.js simulates five falling spheres with contact response. The scene computes a four-second trajectory at fixed steps when restitution changes; Time scrubs the result.

entries.name: d3-voronoi-treemap
entries.purpose: D3 Voronoi Treemap iteratively assigns polygon areas to six weighted leaves. A fixed random seed and bounded iterations make weight changes reproducible.

entries.name: meshoptimizer · Mesh simplification
entries.purpose: Meshoptimizer simplifies an original wavy grid mesh with a geometric error limit. The requested ratio is a target; the error bound may retain more triangles.

entries.name: glsl-solid-wireframe
entries.purpose: Derivative-scaled barycentric edges keep a triangular grid readable at different densities.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: glsl-smooth-min
entries.purpose: The polynomial smooth minimum joins two circles; contour rings expose the changing distance field.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: glsl-sdf-primitives
entries.purpose: Actual sphere, box and torus distance functions drive a bounded ray marcher and finite-difference lighting.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: glsl-ray-sphere
entries.purpose: The library reports sphere intersections. Switch between surface normals and optical path length through the sphere.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: glsl-worley

entries.name: glsl-random
entries.purpose: A GLSL hash gives each integer tile a deterministic value; changing the seed selects another pattern.

entries.name: glsl-lut
entries.purpose: A 64³ color cube packed into a 512² texture warms an original gradient. Strength zero preserves the input.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: glsl-dither
entries.purpose: An 8×8 ordered threshold matrix converts a continuous gradient to discrete dots. Pixel scale exposes the matrix.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: glsl-fxaa
entries.purpose: FXAA filters a deliberately jagged synthetic image. The divider compares original pixels on the left with the filter on the right.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: glsl-fast-gaussian-blur
entries.purpose: The library’s nine-tap filter performs one directional blur pass. Rotate the direction and compare with the original at the left.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: glsl-blend
entries.purpose: Original color fields are combined using the library’s multiply, screen, overlay and difference operations.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: glsl-aastep
entries.purpose: Compare hard thresholding on the left with derivative-smoothed concentric rings on the right.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: glsl-halftone
entries.purpose: The original shader converts an analytic RGB field into rotated CMYK dot screens with simplex-noise paper variation.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: glsl-specular-blinn-phong
entries.purpose: The library evaluates the half-vector specular term on an analytic sphere. Shininess controls the highlight width.
entries.notes: Original GLSL compiled into this on-demand example; full licenses in assets/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt. No model download.

entries.name: NURBS-Python (geomdl)
entries.purpose: Geomdl evaluates a quadratic rational curve at three middle-point weights. These are locally computed samples.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: MuJoCo
entries.purpose: MuJoCo integrates a two-link pendulum with damping. Time selects a locally simulated frame, not a new browser simulation.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: PyVista
entries.purpose: PyVista clips an original torus at three planes. Rotate the prepared meshes to inspect the open cut.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: VTK
entries.purpose: VTK Flying Edges extracts three isosurfaces from a sampled gyroid field. The geometry was computed locally with VTK.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: PROJ
entries.purpose: PROJ, through pyproj, transforms a synthetic geographic grid into Mollweide and Mercator coordinates. No map tiles are downloaded.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: FiPy
entries.purpose: FiPy solves one-dimensional diffusion with zero-flux boundaries. The prepared profiles conserve the initial mass.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: NEURON
entries.purpose: NEURON simulates a Hodgkin–Huxley membrane under three current pulses. The voltage traces are locally generated model outputs.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: healpy
entries.purpose: Healpy evaluates HEALPix pixel centers at three resolutions. Colors mark a synthetic spherical wave.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: Skan
entries.purpose: Skan extracts paths and branch lengths from an original one-pixel-wide skeleton. Highlight a branch to inspect its topology.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: Taichi
entries.purpose: Taichi CPU kernels evolve a discrete heat field. Stored snapshots show diffusion while retaining total heat.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: Datashader
entries.purpose: Datashader bins 100,000 deterministic points at three raster resolutions. Every aggregation accounts for all input points.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: VTracer
entries.purpose: VTracer converts an original binary drawing to SVG. FontTools samples the returned Bézier paths for display; both conversion modes are prepared locally.
entries.notes: Locally executed recipe; prepared result is downloaded with the example. Viewing does not install Python packages.

entries.name: U2-Net
entries.purpose: U²Netp runs through ONNX Runtime on the CPU and extracts a foreground mask from an original procedural flower. This saved prediction includes part of the shadow; compare it with the input.
entries.gpu: Not required for this U2Netp ONNX example; CPU verified.
entries.notes: 4.6 MB weights downloaded and cached only when the recipe runs. Prepared images are downloaded with the example.

entries.name: nanoGPT
entries.purpose: The original nanoGPT model trains locally for 181 steps on three original sentences. The saved curve is training loss, not a generalization score; the text is a sample from the final checkpoint.
entries.notes: Locally executed CPU recipe. Original model.py and MIT license are included.

entries.name: TorchCFM
entries.purpose: TorchCFM samples a noisy conditional path between a Gaussian cloud and a ring. Arrows are target conditional velocities; no learned model or pretrained weights are involved.
entries.notes: Locally executed CPU recipe.

entries.name: Ultralytics YOLO
entries.purpose: YOLO11n-cls classifies an original synthetic flower on the CPU. Its top guess is wrong: inspect the real top-five probabilities rather than treating the labels as truth.
entries.notes: Locally executed CPU recipe.
